artworks.title: Oceanus of the Trevi Fountain
artworks.description: Colossal marble statue of Oceanus presiding over the central niche of the Trevi Fountain in Rome, carved by Pietro Bracci to Nicola Salvi's design. The sea Titan rides a shell-shaped chariot drawn by winged sea-horses — one calm, one restive — guided by tritons, an allegory of the ocean's changing moods.

artworks.title: Oceanus and Tethys (Zeugma mosaic)
artworks.description: Roman floor mosaic from the ancient city of Zeugma on the Euphrates, now in the Zeugma Mosaic Museum in Gaziantep, Turkey. It portrays Oceanus beside his consort Tethys amid fish and sea creatures, an image of the world-encircling river the Greeks imagined girdling the earth.

popCulture.title: Ocean
popCulture.description: English ocean descends from Oceanus — the world-river Titan who became the ordinary word for the open sea.

popCulture.title: Oceanus
popCulture.description: Cartographers and poets kept Oceanus as the encircling water at the edge of the world-map — the Titan as the rim of ancient geography.
